correctness.rationale: For every odd n>=3 and 1<=lambda<=sec(pi/n), each translated polygon lies in a support half-plane <x,v_j> >= eps=1-lambda cos(pi/n); a cyclic Voronoi-sector five-vertex convex containment proves coverage at every point with max_j <x,v_j> >= eps. The uncovered complement is exactly the interior of (sec(pi/n)-lambda)(-P_n); its boundary is covered. Direct area gives n tan(pi/n)(1-lambda cos(pi/n))^2, Hausdorff deficit eps, and n->infty asymptotic pi^5/(4n^4). >=cutoff follows by Minkowski addition. My independently sampled planar half-plane/union check covered 15 nondegenerate triples, 15000 points; the sector proof is infinite in n and real lambda. The regime lambda<1 is excluded.

It determines deficit area and Euclidean Hausdorff distance simultaneously for every odd regular polygon and intermediate dilation, including the precise boundary, not a mechanically repeated threshold result.
